name: Non-text Content
description: All non-text content has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose.

name: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
description: For prerecorded audio-only and prerecorded video-only media, alternatives are provided.

name: Captions (Prerecorded)
description: Captions are provided for all prerecorded audio content in synchronized media.

name: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
description: An alternative for time-based media or audio description of the prerecorded video content is provided.

name: Captions (Live)
description: Captions are provided for all live audio content in synchronized media.

name: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
description: Audio description is provided for all prerecorded video content in synchronized media.
techniques: Add audio description track to video player

name: Sign Language (Prerecorded)
description: Sign language interpretation is provided for all prerecorded audio content in synchronized media.

name: Extended Audio Description (Prerecorded)
description: Where pauses in foreground audio are insufficient to allow audio descriptions, extended audio description is provided.
techniques: Pause video to provide extended descriptions

name: Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
description: An alternative for time-based media is provided for all prerecorded synchronized media and all prerecorded video-only media.
techniques: Provide full text transcript of media

name: Audio-only (Live)
description: An alternative for time-based media that presents equivalent information for live audio-only content is provided.
techniques: Provide real-time text alternative for live audio

name: Info and Relationships
description: Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined or are available in text.
techniques: Use th and scope for table headers

name: Meaningful Sequence
description: When the sequence in which content is presented affects its meaning, a correct reading sequence can be programmatically determined.
techniques: Ensure DOM order matches visual order

name: Sensory Characteristics
description: Instructions provided for understanding and operating content do not rely solely on sensory characteristics of components.
techniques: Don't use color alone to convey info

name: Orientation
description: Content does not restrict its view and operation to a single display orientation unless essential.
techniques: Don't lock orientation via CSS or JS

name: Identify Input Purpose
description: The purpose of each input field collecting information about the user can be programmatically determined.
techniques: Use autocomplete attribute on input fields
Match autocomplete values to input purpose

name: Identify Purpose
description: The purpose of user interface components, icons, and regions can be programmatically determined.

name: Use of Color
description: Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element.
techniques: Add text labels or patterns alongside color

name: Audio Control
description: If any audio on a Web page plays automatically for more than 3 seconds, a mechanism is available to pause/stop or control volume.

name: Contrast (Minimum)
description: The visual presentation of text and images of text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text).
techniques: Ensure 3:1 for large text (18pt+ or 14pt+ bold)

name: Resize Text
description: Text can be resized without assistive technology up to 200 percent without loss of content or functionality.
techniques: Don't use fixed pixel sizes for text

name: Images of Text
description: If the technologies being used can achieve the visual presentation, text is used to convey information rather than images of text.
techniques: Use CSS for text styling instead of images
Use SVG for logos with text alternatives

name: Contrast (Enhanced)
description: The visual presentation of text and images of text has a contrast ratio of at least 7:1 (4.5:1 for large text).
techniques: Use 7:1 contrast ratio for normal text

name: Low or No Background Audio
description: For prerecorded audio-only content that contains primarily speech, background sounds are at least 20 dB lower than the foreground.
techniques: Provide option to turn off background audio

name: Visual Presentation
description: For the visual presentation of blocks of text, foreground/background colors can be selected, width is no more than 80 characters, text is not justified, line spacing is at least 1.5, and paragraph spacing is at least 1.5x line spacing.
techniques: Limit line length to 80 characters (use max-width: 80ch)

name: Images of Text (No Exception)
description: Images of text are only used for pure decoration or where a particular presentation of text is essential.
techniques: Use real text instead of images of text

name: Reflow
description: Content can be presented without loss of information or functionality, and without requiring scrolling in two dimensions at 320 CSS px wide and 256 CSS px tall.

name: Non-text Contrast
description: The visual presentation of UI components and graphical objects has a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors.
techniques: Ensure 3:1 contrast for borders, icons, charts

name: Text Spacing
description: No loss of content or functionality occurs when users override text spacing (line height 1.5x, paragraph spacing 2x, letter spacing 0.12em, word spacing 0.16em).
techniques: Don't use fixed heights on text containers
Allow text to reflow with increased spacing

name: Content on Hover or Focus
description: Where additional content appears on hover or focus, it is dismissible, hoverable, and persistent until dismissed.
techniques: Don't remove on pointer movement within tooltip

name: Keyboard
description: All functionality of the content is operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings.
techniques: Use native interactive elements (button, a, input)
Add tabindex='0' for custom interactive elements
Add keyboard event handlers alongside click handlers

name: No Keyboard Trap
description: If keyboard focus can be moved to a component, focus can be moved away from that component using only a keyboard.
techniques: Ensure all interactive elements can lose focus
Implement proper focus trap only for modals
Allow Escape key to close modals

name: Keyboard (No Exception)
description: All functionality of the content is operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes.
techniques: Make ALL functionality keyboard accessible without exception

name: Character Key Shortcuts
description: If a keyboard shortcut uses only letter, punctuation, number, or symbol characters, it can be turned off, remapped, or is only active on focus.
techniques: Use modifier keys (Ctrl, Alt) with shortcuts
Activate shortcuts only when component is focused

name: Timing Adjustable
description: For each time limit set by content, the user can turn off, adjust, or extend the time limit.
techniques: Provide option to disable time limits

name: Pause, Stop, Hide
description: For moving, blinking, scrolling, or auto-updating information, a mechanism is provided to pause, stop, or hide it.

name: No Timing
description: Timing is not an essential part of the event or activity presented by the content.
techniques: Remove all time limits except for real-time events

name: Interruptions
description: Interruptions can be postponed or suppressed by the user.
techniques: Allow users to suppress non-emergency notifications

name: Re-authenticating
description: When an authenticated session expires, the user can continue the activity without loss of data after re-authenticating.
techniques: Save form data before session timeout

name: Timeouts
description: Users are warned of the duration of any user inactivity that could cause data loss, unless the data is preserved for more than 20 hours.
techniques: Preserve data for at least 20 hours

name: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
description: Web pages do not contain anything that flashes more than three times in any one second period.
techniques: Limit flashing to max 3 per second

name: Three Flashes
description: Web pages do not contain anything that flashes more than three times in any one second period.

name: Animation from Interactions
description: Motion animation triggered by interaction can be disabled, unless the animation is essential.
techniques: Provide setting to disable interaction animations

name: Bypass Blocks
description: A mechanism is available to bypass blocks of content that are repeated on multiple Web pages.

name: Page Titled
description: Web pages have titles that describe topic or purpose.
techniques: Update title on SPA route changes

name: Focus Order
description: If a Web page can be navigated sequentially, components receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability.
techniques: Manage focus when content changes dynamically

name: Link Purpose (In Context)
description: The purpose of each link can be determined from the link text alone or together with its context.

name: Multiple Ways
description: More than one way is available to locate a Web page within a set of Web pages.

name: Headings and Labels
description: Headings and labels describe topic or purpose.

name: Focus Visible
description: Any keyboard operable user interface has a mode of operation where the keyboard focus indicator is visible.

name: Location
description: Information about the user's location within a set of Web pages is available.

name: Link Purpose (Link Only)
description: A mechanism is available to allow the purpose of each link to be identified from link text alone.

name: Section Headings
description: Section headings are used to organize the content.
techniques: Use headings to organize all content sections

name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
description: When a user interface component receives keyboard focus, the component is not entirely hidden due to author-created content.
techniques: Ensure focused element is not behind sticky headers/footers
Account for sticky elements with scroll-padding

name: Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)
description: When a user interface component receives keyboard focus, no part of the component is hidden due to author-created content.
techniques: Ensure no part of focused element is obscured

name: Focus Appearance
description: Focus indicators have sufficient size and contrast.
techniques: Use outline with at least 2px width

name: Pointer Gestures
description: All functionality that uses multipoint or path-based gestures can be operated with a single pointer without a path-based gesture.

name: Pointer Cancellation
description: For functionality that can be operated using a single pointer, at least one is true: up-event, abort/undo, reversal, essential.
techniques: Allow users to cancel accidental clicks by moving pointer away

name: Label in Name
description: For user interface components with labels that include text or images of text, the name contains the text that is presented visually.
techniques: Ensure aria-label starts with visible text
Match accessible name to visible label

name: Motion Actuation
description: Functionality that can be operated by device motion or user motion can also be operated by user interface components.
techniques: Provide UI controls for motion-activated features
Allow users to disable motion actuation

name: Target Size (Enhanced)
description: The size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels.
techniques: Add padding to small interactive elements

name: Dragging Movements
description: All functionality that uses a dragging movement for operation can be achieved by a single pointer without dragging.
techniques: Provide click/tap alternatives to drag operations
Add move up/down buttons for sortable lists

name: Target Size (Minimum)
description: The size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels.

name: Language of Page
description: The default human language of each Web page can be programmatically determined.
techniques: Set lang attribute on html element

name: Language of Parts
description: The human language of each passage or phrase in the content can be programmatically determined.
techniques: Use lang attribute on elements with different language text

name: Unusual Words
description: A mechanism is available for identifying definitions of words or phrases used in an unusual or restricted way.

name: Abbreviations
description: A mechanism for identifying the expanded form or meaning of abbreviations is available.

name: Reading Level
description: When text requires more than a lower secondary education reading level, supplemental content or a version is available.

name: Pronunciation
description: A mechanism is available for identifying pronunciation of words where meaning is ambiguous without knowing pronunciation.
techniques: Use ruby annotation for complex characters

name: On Focus
description: When any user interface component receives focus, it does not initiate a change of context.
techniques: Don't change context on tab/focus events

name: On Input
description: Changing the setting of any user interface component does not automatically cause a change of context unless the user has been advised beforehand.
techniques: Use submit buttons for form submission

name: Consistent Navigation
description: Navigational mechanisms that are repeated on multiple Web pages occur in the same relative order each time.
techniques: Keep nav in same position across pages

name: Consistent Identification
description: Components that have the same functionality within a set of Web pages are identified consistently.
techniques: Use same labels for same functions

name: Change on Request
description: Changes of context are initiated only by user request, or a mechanism is available to turn off such changes.
techniques: Only change context on explicit user action

name: Consistent Help
description: If a Web page contains help mechanisms, they occur in the same relative order on each page.
techniques: Place help links/chat in consistent location
Use same help mechanism across pages

name: Error Identification
description: If an input error is automatically detected, the item that is in error is identified and the error is described to the user in text.
techniques: Show error messages next to fields

name: Labels or Instructions
description: Labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input.
techniques: Use visible labels for all inputs
Use placeholder as supplement, not replacement for label

name: Error Suggestion
description: If an input error is automatically detected and suggestions are known, they are provided to the user.
techniques: Provide expected format in error message

name: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
description: For pages that cause legal commitments or financial transactions, submissions are reversible, checked, or confirmed.
techniques: Use confirmation dialogs for irreversible actions

name: Help
description: Context-sensitive help is available.

name: Error Prevention (All)
description: For all user submissions, submissions are reversible, checked, or confirmed.
techniques: Provide confirmation for all form submissions

name: Redundant Entry
description: Information previously entered by the user is either auto-populated or available for selection.

name: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
description: A cognitive function test is not required for any step of authentication unless an alternative or assistance is provided.

name: Accessible Authentication (Enhanced)
description: A cognitive function test is not required for any step of authentication.

name: Parsing
description: In content implemented using markup languages, elements have complete start and end tags, are nested according to spec, don't contain duplicate attributes, and IDs are unique. (Obsolete in WCAG 2.2)

name: Name, Role, Value
description: For all user interface components, the name and role can be programmatically determined; states, properties, and values can be programmatically set.
techniques: Use native HTML elements when possible
Add ARIA roles for custom widgets
Update aria-expanded, aria-selected as state changes

name: Status Messages
description: In content implemented using markup languages, status messages can be programmatically determined through role or properties so they can be presented to the user by assistive technologies without receiving focus.
techniques: Use aria-live regions for dynamic content updates
